claims.statement: Poland's official KSeF guidance states that receipt through KSeF became mandatory on 1 February 2026, issuing became mandatory for most remaining taxpayers on 1 April 2026, and firms at or below PLN 10,000 of monthly invoiced gross sales remain exempt from issuing only through the end of 2026.
The Ministry of Finance says monetary penalties for KSeF usage errors are not imposed for 2026, reducing immediate penalty-led urgency even though the operating transition is live.

Inference: a trade-specific closeout layer may be sellable where free government tools and general accounting products handle the tax document but not the upstream field evidence and milestone workflow.

contrary_evidence: The Ministry provides free taxpayer, mobile, and e-microfirm tools, and many accounting vendors already integrate with KSeF.
The absence of monetary penalties for 2026 may let the smallest firms postpone paid workflow improvements.
The smallest exempt firms may also have the lowest software budgets and highest churn.

economics.acquisition_route: One parent-company design partner, then paid referrals and white-label seats sold through bookkeeping offices and trade wholesalers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 4,000 firms at PLN 3,600 annual recurring revenue yields PLN 14.4m revenue; at a 40% operating margin, six years of retained profit and distributions after scale could plausibly build PLN 20m-plus founder net worth without a sale
economics.founder_time: Approximately three hours per day for product and exception analysis plus one hour for channel and pilot support until support can be delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software validation and monitoring should exceed 80% gross margin after onboarding; founder- or bookkeeper-led setup would initially be materially lower margin
economics.payback: Target one to four months because setup revenue is intended to cover configuration and channel commission
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 900-2,500 onboarding, PLN 149-499 per month, and PLN 1-3 per submitted invoice
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly invoicing and recurring job templates create habitual use; retention weakens if accounting suites absorb the field-closeout workflow

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A proprietary corpus linking trade-specific job events, contract milestones, VAT treatments, and returned invoice exceptions to reusable closeout templates for each installation trade
fingerprint.customer: Polish renewable-energy, HVAC, and electrical contractors with two to twenty field workers, including firms below the temporary PLN 10,000 monthly invoiced-sales exemption and larger firms already issuing through KSeF
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot in the founder's parents' seven-person renewable installer, then template-led resale through bookkeeping offices, electrical wholesalers, and existing field-service software vendors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Vertical workflow SaaS that captures acceptance protocols and milestone evidence, validates required invoice fields, hands an FA(3)-ready payload to an authorised KSeF/accounting connector, and monitors identifiers and offline exceptions; paid onboarding plus subscription and usage
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The contractor or its bookkeeping office pays a setup fee when its first job template and KSeF permissions are configured, then a monthly and per-document fee when accepted job closeouts enter the invoice queue
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Mandatory KSeF receipt began on 1 February 2026; most issuing began on 1 April 2026; the temporarily exempt smallest firms must issue through KSeF from 1 January 2027, forcing field-service firms to replace informal photo-and-spreadsheet handoffs

founder_fit: The parents' installer provides a low-cost, high-fidelity pilot without cold outbound
Schema validation, exception classification, and workflow automation match data-science skills
A self-serve trade template can be built in bounded daily blocks alongside employment
Bookkeeping and wholesaler channels reduce dependence on a public persona or constant meetings
risks: Mishandled KSeF credentials or permissions could expose sensitive invoice data.
Tax-rule errors could create customer losses despite positioning the product as workflow software rather than tax advice.
A Poland-only tax interface creates concentration risk unless the field-closeout asset later supports other mandates.
High exception volume could turn a bounded SaaS into an unscalable support service.

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical field-workflow SaaS with transaction-metered compliance handoff
structure.control_point: The signed-job-to-KSeF release gate where operational evidence becomes an invoice payload
structure.critical_dependency: Stable KSeF authentication and API behaviour plus permissioned integration with an accountant or invoicing connector

thesis: A narrow job-closeout-to-invoice layer for Polish renewable, HVAC, and electrical contractors can turn signed protocols, site photos, milestone terms, and VAT metadata into validated KSeF-ready invoice payloads and an exception queue. The wedge is the last group of very small firms approaching the 1 January 2027 issuing deadline, while already-covered contractors still need a reliable bridge between field evidence and accounting rather than another general ledger.
title: KSeF Field-Service Closeout Ledger for Polish Installation Crews
uncertainties: No evidence yet shows that contractors will pay for field-closeout integration rather than change their bookkeeping process manually.
The representative frequency of milestone, retention, correction, and offline cases must be measured in the parent-company pilot.
The 4,000-customer wealth scenario and channel conversion assumptions are unvalidated.
Whether accountants will resell the tool or view it as added support burden is unknown.
